# HELP fros_info Constant 1; labels identify this router (site name, hostname, version, release codename).
# TYPE fros_info gauge
fros_info{site_name="edge-gw",hostname="edge-gw",version="0.2.1",codename="Ice Breaker"} 1
# HELP fros_config_valid 1 if the on-disk config.yaml passes validation, else 0.
# TYPE fros_config_valid gauge
fros_config_valid 1
# HELP fros_interface_bytes_total Total bytes transferred per network interface and direction.
# TYPE fros_interface_bytes_total counter
# HELP fros_xdp_status XDP TLS SNI filter attach status per interface (0=disabled/not attached, 1=native, 2=generic).
# TYPE fros_xdp_status gauge
fros_xdp_status{device="eth1"} 0
fros_xdp_status{device="eth2"} 0
# HELP fros_iot_devices Devices found by the last IoT scan, by classification.
# TYPE fros_iot_devices gauge
fros_iot_devices{category="iot"} 1
fros_iot_devices{category="general"} 0
fros_iot_devices{category="unknown"} 0
# HELP fros_iot_isolated_devices Devices currently isolated by MAC address in the kernel iot_isolated set.
# TYPE fros_iot_isolated_devices gauge
fros_iot_isolated_devices 12345678901234567890
# HELP fros_dns_blocked_domains Domains currently loaded into the DNS resolver, per blocklist category.
# TYPE fros_dns_blocked_domains gauge
fros_dns_blocked_domains{category="ads"} 0
fros_dns_blocked_domains{category="malware"} 0
fros_dns_blocked_domains{category="my-list"} 0
# HELP fros_app_active_clients Clients that used the app in the last 15 minutes (DNS lookups / TLS SNIs).
# TYPE fros_app_active_clients gauge
fros_app_active_clients{app="youtube",category="streaming"} 0
fros_app_active_clients{app="zz-unknown",category="unknown"} 1
# HELP fros_app_hits_24h DNS lookups and TLS connections attributed to the app in the last 24 hours.
# TYPE fros_app_hits_24h gauge
fros_app_hits_24h{app="youtube",category="streaming"} 0
fros_app_hits_24h{app="zz-unknown",category="unknown"} 7.0
# HELP fros_app_blocked Apps currently on the blocked list (1 per blocked app).
# TYPE fros_app_blocked gauge
fros_app_blocked{app="tiktok"} 1
# HELP fros_tls_fingerprinted_clients Clients with at least one TLS fingerprint recorded.
# TYPE fros_tls_fingerprinted_clients gauge
fros_tls_fingerprinted_clients 2
# HELP fros_tls_distinct_fingerprints Distinct JA4 fingerprints recorded across all clients.
# TYPE fros_tls_distinct_fingerprints gauge
fros_tls_distinct_fingerprints 3
# HELP fros_tls_fingerprint_events_24h TLS fingerprint events in the last 24 hours, by type.
# TYPE fros_tls_fingerprint_events_24h gauge
fros_tls_fingerprint_events_24h{type="new_fingerprint"} 0
fros_tls_fingerprint_events_24h{type="blocklist"} 1
# HELP fros_xdp_blocked_connections_total Total connections dropped by the XDP TLS SNI filter for matching the blocklist.
# TYPE fros_xdp_blocked_connections_total counter
fros_xdp_blocked_connections_total 12.0
# HELP fros_adblock_total_domains Number of unique domains currently in the ad-block hosts list.
# TYPE fros_adblock_total_domains gauge
fros_adblock_total_domains 0
# HELP fros_ztna_active_sessions Number of currently authorized ZTNA client sessions.
# TYPE fros_ztna_active_sessions gauge
fros_ztna_active_sessions 2.5
# HELP fros_bruteforce_banned_ips Number of source IPs currently banned in the brute-force jail.
# TYPE fros_bruteforce_banned_ips gauge
fros_bruteforce_banned_ips 1
# HELP fros_ai_ids_quarantined_hosts Number of hosts currently quarantined by the AI IDS/IPS engine.
# TYPE fros_ai_ids_quarantined_hosts gauge
fros_ai_ids_quarantined_hosts 0
# HELP fros_hw_cpu_info CPU model identification (value is always 1).
# TYPE fros_hw_cpu_info gauge
# HELP fros_hw_cpu_usage_ratio Current CPU utilization ratio (0-1), sampled over a short interval.
# TYPE fros_hw_cpu_usage_ratio gauge
# HELP fros_hw_cpu_mhz Current CPU clock speed in MHz.
# TYPE fros_hw_cpu_mhz gauge
# HELP fros_hw_ram_info Installed RAM module identification (value is always 1); requires root via dmidecode.
# TYPE fros_hw_ram_info gauge
# HELP fros_hw_ram_usage_bytes Currently used RAM in bytes (MemTotal - MemAvailable).
# TYPE fros_hw_ram_usage_bytes gauge
fros_hw_ram_usage_bytes 768000
# HELP fros_hw_ram_total_bytes Total installed RAM in bytes.
# TYPE fros_hw_ram_total_bytes gauge
fros_hw_ram_total_bytes 1024000
# HELP fros_hw_storage_info Mounted storage device identification (value is always 1).
# TYPE fros_hw_storage_info gauge
fros_hw_storage_info{mount="/",device_name="/dev/sda1"} 1
# HELP fros_hw_storage_usage_bytes Used storage space in bytes for this mount.
# TYPE fros_hw_storage_usage_bytes gauge
fros_hw_storage_usage_bytes{mount="/"} 2147483648
# HELP fros_hw_storage_total_bytes Total storage space in bytes for this mount.
# TYPE fros_hw_storage_total_bytes gauge
fros_hw_storage_total_bytes{mount="/"} 8589934592

FR_OSNetworkSegments

Network segments

On one flat network, a hacked camera or a guest's infected laptop can reach every other device. A segment is a separate network with its own addresses and DHCP that can reach the internet and nothing else. Each one here is a VLAN on the LAN port (eth1): set your access point to put the IoT and guest Wi-Fi on these VLAN IDs (or use a VLAN-capable switch).

SegmentVLANNetworkDevice
IoT devices (iot) 30 192.168.30.1/24 eth1.30
Guests (guest) 40 192.168.40.1/24 eth1.40

Each gets DHCP (.100-.199, public DNS), a rule to the internet and nothing towards your LAN or this router's management. IoT devices are also inventoried and isolated (see IoT Devices).

Firewall rules

Evaluated in order, first match wins. "self" as a zone means the router itself. Scheduled drop/reject rules that cut open connections are evaluated before all other rules.

No problems found -- no any-to-any or internet-wide accept rules, nothing shadowed, nothing unused for 90 days.

FR_OSProtectionAd-Block

Ad-Block & DNS Filtering

Downloads blocklists (hosts files or plain domain lists), dedupes them, and serves the result from a dedicated, frfw-managed DNS resolver (dnsmasq). Each category is kept as its own list, so blocks and counts can be told apart. Optionally also pushes a small "critical" subset of the base list into the existing Phase 4 XDP kernel filter.

Enabled, not yet applied -- run Apply
Domains loaded
0
ads
0
malware
0
my-list
0

Base list

Suggested: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StevenBlack/hosts/master/hosts

Feeds up to this many base-list domains into the existing TLS SNI filter's kernel blocklist -- only takes effect if that filter is also enabled; leave at 0 to keep everything DNS-side.

Categories

Each list's own license and terms apply -- check them before use in a business.

Custom categories from config.yaml (kept as they are):

  • my-list: https://lists.example/mine, https://lists.example/mine2

LAN DNS

Local names

Names the router's resolver answers itself, for the clients it serves (needs Enabled and "Serve DHCP clients" above). A host is one exact name; an override also covers every subdomain, e.g. an internal server for a public name. They are never sent upstream and never blocked.

No local names yet.

Refresh

Downloads and dedupes the configured lists right now, instead of waiting for the daily fr-adblock-refresh.timer. Can take a while depending on list size and network speed.

System: Post-Quantum Hybrid Key Exchange

Hardens the management layer (this webUI's HTTPS listener, and this host's sshd if installed) with a hybrid classical+PQC key exchange (X25519MLKEM768 for TLS, mlkem768x25519-sha256 for SSH), falling back to classical-only automatically on any client or host build that doesn't support it yet.

Enabled, not yet active
PQC enabled in config
Yes
Host OpenSSL
Go crypto/tls (X25519MLKEM768)
SSH installed
No

TLS (webUI HTTPS)

CheckResult
Host OpenSSL supports X25519MLKEM768 (requires OpenSSL ≥ 3.5) Yes
Last applied TLS group preference (never applied)
Hybrid group currently applied No

TLS 1.3 is always enforced when PQC is enabled below. The group preference itself only takes effect on the next apply and a subsequent systemctl restart fr-webui -- OpenSSL reads its configuration once, at process start.

SSH

sshd is not installed on this host -- nothing to configure.

Settings

Never breaks an older client or an older sshd/browser build -- if the host's OpenSSL or OpenSSH is too old to know the hybrid algorithm name, this silently keeps the classical-only fallback list (still TLS 1.3-only on the webUI side) instead of failing.

Management access

The webUI and SSH listen on 127.0.0.1 and are reachable from no zone (console only).

To manage the router from outside, turn on the VPN (WireGuard) rather than opening the webUI and SSH to the internet.

Which zones count as management: management.zones in the config (default: every zone that isn't internet-facing).

webUI address

Where the webUI and SSH listen (besides the router itself). Only this setting moves them: a change elsewhere that would take one of these addresses away is refused (ROADMAP SEC-27). Saving applies it at once, held until you confirm it from the new address within 300 s; otherwise the router goes back.

No management interface has a static address: the webUI is reachable from the router itself only.

Over IPv6

The webUI and SSH can also listen on the router's stable IPv6 address (ULA) in each management zone that has IPv6 -- never on the provider's addresses, which change and are public. The same rules apply as over IPv4.

IPv6 is off (Interfaces screen).

Software integrity

FR_OS's files -- the program, its compiled files, its systemd units and scripts, the XDP program -- are compared with the signed release they came from (security-lessons G9, ROADMAP SEC-15), so rewriting pip's install record doesn't hide a change. It covers FR_OS's own files only: a change elsewhere -- another systemd unit, another program, an SSH key -- is not reported. Someone with root can still change this check itself: the check that doesn't trust the router reads its boot medium from another computer (scripts/verify-medium.py).

not verifiable FR_OS 2 keeps no list of its files' hashes yet

Storage & persistence

installed This router runs from its own disk; every change is kept.

Multi-site monitoring

A Prometheus server can scrape this router's /metrics over HTTPS. It is off until a token is generated here; then it answers only requests carrying Authorization: Bearer <token> (only its SHA-256 is kept in config.yaml). Examples: telemetry/prometheus-multisite.yml and the fleet dashboard in telemetry/.

Token: none -- /metrics is off

IPv6

The router takes IPv6 from the provider on its internet-facing interfaces: an address (SLAAC or DHCPv6) and, if the provider delegates one, a prefix. Each LAN zone's interface gets a /64 network of that prefix, which its devices configure themselves from (SLAAC; ipv6.lan_zones chooses the zones, all of them by default). Each also gets a stable network of the router's own (ULA), where the router answers DNS whatever the provider gives. The rules decide what the LAN reaches over IPv6, as over IPv4; nothing new comes in from the internet but through a pinhole (ipv6.pinholes). The webUI and SSH answer over IPv6 only with management.ipv6, on the stable address.

FR_OSNetworkSegments

Network segments

On one flat network, a hacked camera or a guest's infected laptop can reach every other device. A segment is a separate network with its own addresses and DHCP that can reach the internet and nothing else. Each one here is a VLAN on the LAN port (?): set your access point to put the IoT and guest Wi-Fi on these VLAN IDs (or use a VLAN-capable switch).

SegmentVLANNetworkDevice
IoT devices (iot) 30 192.168.30.1/24 -
Guests (guest) 40 192.168.40.1/24 -

Each gets DHCP (.100-.199, public DNS), a rule to the internet and nothing towards your LAN or this router's management. IoT devices are also inventoried and isolated (see IoT Devices).

Ad-Block & DNS Filtering

Downloads blocklists (hosts files or plain domain lists), dedupes them, and serves the result from a dedicated, frfw-managed DNS resolver (dnsmasq). Each category is kept as its own list, so blocks and counts can be told apart. Optionally also pushes a small "critical" subset of the base list into the existing Phase 4 XDP kernel filter.

Base list

Suggested: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StevenBlack/hosts/master/hosts

Feeds up to this many base-list domains into the existing TLS SNI filter's kernel blocklist -- only takes effect if that filter is also enabled; leave at 0 to keep everything DNS-side.

Categories

Each list's own license and terms apply -- check them before use in a business.

LAN DNS

Local names

Names the router's resolver answers itself, for the clients it serves (needs Enabled and "Serve DHCP clients" above). A host is one exact name; an override also covers every subdomain, e.g. an internal server for a public name. They are never sent upstream and never blocked.

No local names yet.

Refresh

Downloads and dedupes the configured lists right now, instead of waiting for the daily fr-adblock-refresh.timer. Can take a while depending on list size and network speed.

FR_OSSystemSystem

System: Post-Quantum Hybrid Key Exchange

Hardens the management layer (this webUI's HTTPS listener, and this host's sshd if installed) with a hybrid classical+PQC key exchange (X25519MLKEM768 for TLS, mlkem768x25519-sha256 for SSH), falling back to classical-only automatically on any client or host build that doesn't support it yet.

Classical only
PQC enabled in config
No
Host OpenSSL
Go crypto/tls (X25519MLKEM768)
SSH installed
No

TLS (webUI HTTPS)

CheckResult
Host OpenSSL supports X25519MLKEM768 (requires OpenSSL ≥ 3.5) Yes
Last applied TLS group preference (never applied)
Hybrid group currently applied No

TLS 1.3 is always enforced when PQC is enabled below. The group preference itself only takes effect on the next apply and a subsequent systemctl restart fr-webui -- OpenSSL reads its configuration once, at process start.

SSH

sshd is not installed on this host -- nothing to configure.

Settings

Never breaks an older client or an older sshd/browser build -- if the host's OpenSSL or OpenSSH is too old to know the hybrid algorithm name, this silently keeps the classical-only fallback list (still TLS 1.3-only on the webUI side) instead of failing.

Management access

management.allow_wan is on: the webUI and SSH are reachable from the internet. Use the WireGuard VPN (VPN screen) for remote management instead and turn this off.

The webUI and SSH listen on 0.0.0.0 and are reachable from the lan, vpn, wan zone(s).

Away from home, manage the router through the VPN: it is on -- tick its tunnel address under "webUI address" below to have the webUI and SSH listen there too. There is no need to open them to the internet as well -- turn that off below.

Which zones count as management: management.zones in the config (default: every zone that isn't internet-facing).

webUI address

Where the webUI and SSH listen (besides the router itself). Only this setting moves them: a change elsewhere that would take one of these addresses away is refused (ROADMAP SEC-27). Saving applies it at once, held until you confirm it from the new address within 300 s; otherwise the router goes back.

Over IPv6

The webUI and SSH can also listen on the router's stable IPv6 address (ULA) in each management zone that has IPv6 -- never on the provider's addresses, which change and are public. The same rules apply as over IPv4.

IPv6 is off (Interfaces screen).

Software integrity

FR_OS's files -- the program, its compiled files, its systemd units and scripts, the XDP program -- are compared with the signed release they came from (security-lessons G9, ROADMAP SEC-15), so rewriting pip's install record doesn't hide a change. It covers FR_OS's own files only: a change elsewhere -- another systemd unit, another program, an SSH key -- is not reported. Someone with root can still change this check itself: the check that doesn't trust the router reads its boot medium from another computer (scripts/verify-medium.py).

not verifiable FR_OS 2 keeps no list of its files' hashes yet

Storage & persistence

persistent Live system with persistence on /dev/sdb3, /dev/sdc1: settings, passwords and leases survive reboots.

Boot medium: /dev/sdb1

Multi-site monitoring

A Prometheus server can scrape this router's /metrics over HTTPS. It is off until a token is generated here; then it answers only requests carrying Authorization: Bearer <token> (only its SHA-256 is kept in config.yaml). Examples: telemetry/prometheus-multisite.yml and the fleet dashboard in telemetry/.

Token: none -- /metrics is off

FR_OSNetworkVPN

VPN (WireGuard)

Reach your network -- and manage this router -- from anywhere, with a key per device instead of a password. A stolen password works from anywhere; a WireGuard key only on the device that holds it, and the router only ever knows its public half. This is the safe alternative to opening the webUI to the internet.

On
Tunnel
down
Devices
2
Port
UDP 51821

Settings

Turning it on adds a vpn zone and rules that let the VPN reach the webUI, SSH and the LAN (if they aren't there yet); change them on the Rules screen. Click Apply on the dashboard to load it.

Router's public key: RRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRR=

Devices

NameAddressPublic keyLast handshake
phone 10.99.0.2/32 QQQQQQQQQQQQ... never
laptop 10.99.0.3/32
No IPv6 in its configuration		 MMMMMMMMMMMM... never

A device marked No IPv6 in its configuration was added before the tunnel had IPv6, or with its own key. If its configuration sends all traffic through the VPN, its IPv6 still goes around the tunnel, in the clear on whatever network it is on. Remove it and add it again for a new configuration (a new key: the old private key was never stored), or add its IPv6 address shown here to Address and ::/0 to AllowedIPs on the device. Its old configuration keeps working until then.

FR_OSProtectionIoT Devices

IoT Devices

Discovers devices in the selected zones (DHCP leases, the ARP table and an mDNS service query), classifies them by hardware vendor, advertised services and hostname, and can isolate IoT devices by MAC address in the router's own firewall. Isolation covers everything routed through this box; devices on the same switch/Wi-Fi segment can still reach each other directly -- put IoT gear in its own zone/VLAN for full separation.

version: 1
hostname: fr-router
timezone: Europe/Budapest
interfaces:
  wan:
    device: eth0
    zone: wan
  lan:
    device: eth1
    zone: lan
    address: 192.168.1.1/24
  dmz:
    device: eth2
    zone: dmz
    address: 10.0.2.1/24
zones:
  wan: {}
  lan: {}
  dmz: {}
nat:
  masquerade:
  - out_zone: wan
rules:
- name: lan-to-wan
  action: accept
  from_zone: lan
  to_zone: wan
- name: web
  action: accept
  from_zone: lan
  to_zone: wan
  proto: tcp
  dst_port: 443
  log: true
- name: kids-night
  action: drop
  from_zone: lan
  to_zone: wan
  src_mac: aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:01
  schedule:
    days:
    - weekdays
    start: '21:30'
    end: 06:30
    cut_established: true
- name: weekend
  action: accept
  from_zone: lan
  to_zone: dmz
  schedule:
    days:
    - sat
    - sun
    start: 00:00
    end: '23:59'
- name: old-temp
  action: accept
  from_zone: lan
  to_zone: dmz
  proto: tcp
  dst_port: 8000-8100
  expires: 2026-10-01T12:00
- name: soon
  action: accept
  from_zone: lan
  to_zone: dmz
  proto: udp
  dst_port: 53
  expires: 2026-11-01T09:00
- name: ssh
  action: accept
  from_zone: lan
  to_zone: self
  proto: tcp
  dst_port: 22
  require_ztna: true
- name: everything
  action: accept
- name: dmz-mail
  action: accept
  from_zone: wan
  to_zone: dmz
  proto: tcp
  dst_port: 25
  src_address:
  - 203.0.113.0/24
  - 2001:db8::/32
  dst_address: 10.0.2.25

  action: drop
  from_zone: lan
  to_zone: wan
  proto: tcp
  dst_port: 8080-8090
  src_address:
  - 192.168.1.0/25
  - 2001:db8:1::/48
  log: true
  src_mac: aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:02
  schedule:
    days:
    - mon
    - fri
    start: 08:00
    end: '17:00'
    cut_established: true
  expires: 2026-12-24T18:00

FR_OSNetworkRules

Firewall rules

Evaluated in order, first match wins. "self" as a zone means the router itself. Scheduled drop/reject rules that cut open connections are evaluated before all other rules.

Rule check

RuleFinding
old-temp expired expired: the firewall already ignores it; remove it to keep the list clean
everything any-to-any accepts everything from anywhere to anywhere: the firewall is off for it
open open-from-internet opens all of the dmz zone to the internet (wan): limit it to a port or a source address
dmz-mail redundant redundant: 'everything' above already matches all of it the same way
open redundant redundant: 'everything' above already matches all of it the same way
web redundant redundant: 'lan-to-wan' above already matches all of it the same way

Rule hit counters are recorded hourly (fr-schedule-check.timer); "unused" means no match for 90 days.

lan-to-wan accept lan wan any - - always - - - -

Add rule

Schedule (optional -- leave the times empty for "always")

No day ticked = every day. An end time before the start runs past midnight (22:00-06:00).

Schedule time zone

Rule schedules are in this zone. Router time now: Sun 2026-11-01 01:00 CET. Daylight-saving changes are picked up automatically within the hour (fr-schedule-check.timer).

Ad-Block & DNS Filtering

Downloads blocklists (hosts files or plain domain lists), dedupes them, and serves the result from a dedicated, frfw-managed DNS resolver (dnsmasq). Each category is kept as its own list, so blocks and counts can be told apart. Optionally also pushes a small "critical" subset of the base list into the existing Phase 4 XDP kernel filter.

Domains loaded

Base list

Suggested: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StevenBlack/hosts/master/hosts

Feeds up to this many base-list domains into the existing TLS SNI filter's kernel blocklist -- only takes effect if that filter is also enabled; leave at 0 to keep everything DNS-side.

Categories

Each list's own license and terms apply -- check them before use in a business.

Custom categories from config.yaml (kept as they are):

  • my-list: https://lists.example/mine, https://lists.example/mine2

LAN DNS

Local names

Names the router's resolver answers itself, for the clients it serves (needs Enabled and "Serve DHCP clients" above). A host is one exact name; an override also covers every subdomain, e.g. an internal server for a public name. They are never sent upstream and never blocked.

NameAddressKind
nas.lan192.168.1.10Host
printer.lan192.168.1.11Host
intranet.example192.168.1.12Override (with subdomains)

Refresh

Downloads and dedupes the configured lists right now, instead of waiting for the daily fr-adblock-refresh.timer. Can take a while depending on list size and network speed.

System: Post-Quantum Hybrid Key Exchange

Hardens the management layer (this webUI's HTTPS listener, and this host's sshd if installed) with a hybrid classical+PQC key exchange (X25519MLKEM768 for TLS, mlkem768x25519-sha256 for SSH), falling back to classical-only automatically on any client or host build that doesn't support it yet.

Classical only
PQC enabled in config
No
Host OpenSSL
Go crypto/tls (X25519MLKEM768)
SSH installed
No

TLS (webUI HTTPS)

CheckResult
Host OpenSSL supports X25519MLKEM768 (requires OpenSSL ≥ 3.5) Yes
Last applied TLS group preference (never applied)
Hybrid group currently applied No

TLS 1.3 is always enforced when PQC is enabled below. The group preference itself only takes effect on the next apply and a subsequent systemctl restart fr-webui -- OpenSSL reads its configuration once, at process start.

SSH

sshd is not installed on this host -- nothing to configure.

Settings

Never breaks an older client or an older sshd/browser build -- if the host's OpenSSL or OpenSSH is too old to know the hybrid algorithm name, this silently keeps the classical-only fallback list (still TLS 1.3-only on the webUI side) instead of failing.

Management access

The webUI and SSH listen on 127.0.0.1, 192.168.1.1 and are reachable from the lan, vpn zone(s). The firewall drops them from wan, whatever the rules say.

Away from home, manage the router through the VPN: it is on -- tick its tunnel address under "webUI address" below to have the webUI and SSH listen there too.

Which zones count as management: management.zones in the config (default: every zone that isn't internet-facing).

webUI address

Where the webUI and SSH listen (besides the router itself). Only this setting moves them: a change elsewhere that would take one of these addresses away is refused (ROADMAP SEC-27). Saving applies it at once, held until you confirm it from the new address within 300 s; otherwise the router goes back.

Over IPv6

The webUI and SSH can also listen on the router's stable IPv6 address (ULA) in each management zone that has IPv6 -- never on the provider's addresses, which change and are public. The same rules apply as over IPv4.

IPv6 is off (Interfaces screen).

Software integrity

FR_OS's files -- the program, its compiled files, its systemd units and scripts, the XDP program -- are compared with the signed release they came from (security-lessons G9, ROADMAP SEC-15), so rewriting pip's install record doesn't hide a change. It covers FR_OS's own files only: a change elsewhere -- another systemd unit, another program, an SSH key -- is not reported. Someone with root can still change this check itself: the check that doesn't trust the router reads its boot medium from another computer (scripts/verify-medium.py).

not verifiable FR_OS 2 keeps no list of its files' hashes yet

Storage & persistence

Live system without persistence: every change made since boot -- config, passwords, enabled services -- is lost at the next reboot.

This boot did not use the persistence option. FR_OS creates a persistence partition by itself on the first boot when the USB stick it was written to has at least 256 MiB free after the image. To use an internal disk instead (a read-only medium, a VM's virtual CD): sudo firewall-cli persistence create /dev/sdX --yes, then reboot.

Boot medium: /dev/sdb1

Multi-site monitoring

A Prometheus server can scrape this router's /metrics over HTTPS. It is off until a token is generated here; then it answers only requests carrying Authorization: Bearer <token> (only its SHA-256 is kept in config.yaml). Examples: telemetry/prometheus-multisite.yml and the fleet dashboard in telemetry/.

Token: none -- /metrics is off

Certificate for the scraper's ca_file: download

FR_OSNetworkSegments

Network segments

On one flat network, a hacked camera or a guest's infected laptop can reach every other device. A segment is a separate network with its own addresses and DHCP that can reach the internet and nothing else. Each one here is a VLAN on the LAN port (eth1): set your access point to put the IoT and guest Wi-Fi on these VLAN IDs (or use a VLAN-capable switch).

SegmentVLANNetworkDevice
IoT devices (iot) 30 192.168.30.1/24 eth1.30 set up
Guests (guest) 40 192.168.40.1/24 eth1.40 set up

Each gets DHCP (.100-.199, public DNS), a rule to the internet and nothing towards your LAN or this router's management. IoT devices are also inventoried and isolated (see IoT Devices).

FR_OSProtectionTLS SNI Filter

XDP TLS SNI Filter

Kernel-space (XDP/eBPF) TLS ClientHello inspection -- drops connections to blocklisted domains before they reach the kernel's normal network stack. What it can't see is listed below, and in bpf/xdp_sni_filter.c -- read that before relying on this as a complete filter.

Disabled
Interface
-
Blocked domains
0
Drops (since last load)

What this filter doesn't see

  • QUIC (HTTP/3, UDP/443). Its ClientHello is encrypted. Rejected from the filtered ports and their VLANs once the filter is on and applied.
  • Encrypted Client Hello (ECH). The real name is encrypted; the filter sees only the outer, public one.
  • TLS on ports other than 443.
  • ClientHellos over several TLS records. They pass, counted as truncated. One split across TCP segments is followed: a segment out of order is dropped until TCP sends it in order, one with a bad checksum is dropped unread, and a hello longer than 16 segments, unfinished after 30 seconds or in a segment over 2,048 bytes is dropped.
  • Names of 32 bytes or more. Refused when you add them, so none is silently ineffective.
  • IPv6 with more than four extension headers, and TCP fragments. The filter reads IPv6 like IPv4, behind up to four extension headers. A packet with more, and a TCP fragment of either family, is dropped instead: no LAN device sends one, and the server would put a hello back together that the filter never saw whole.

Settings

XDP only sees packets an interface receives. To filter what LAN clients connect to, pick the LAN-side interfaces; on the WAN interface it only sees connections coming in from the internet.

Blocking a domain also blocks its subdomains (e.g. "example.com" blocks "www.example.com" too) -- see this project's ARCHITECTURE.md for the LPM-trie matching scheme.

Saving only updates config.yaml -- click Apply on the dashboard to actually load the filter into the kernel.

Blocked domains

No domains configured yet.

Live TLS Inspection Logs (40Gbps Wire-Speed Data Plane)

Streamed from fr-xdp-sni-logger's journal as each match is logged -- the drop decision itself already happened in the kernel, entirely independent of this page being open. "40Gbps wire-speed" describes what the native (xdpdrv) data plane is designed for on supported hardware, not a throughput number measured on this box -- see ROADMAP.md's phase 4 open items for real hardware benchmarking status. Status: Connecting…

Waiting for events…

FR_OS v0.2.1 · Ice Breaker fr-router
admin Admin
Core

AI IDS/IPS TLS SNI Filter Ad-Block IoT Devices Applications TLS Fingerprints ZTNA Gate

Update System Attack surface Security score Users
FR_OSProtectionApplications

Applications

Recognises which apps clients use from the names they look up through the router's resolver and, optionally, the TLS server names (SNI) the XDP filter sees -- nothing is decrypted. A "hit" is one lookup or one TLS connection, a rough activity signal, not traffic volume. Apps are blocked by the resolver answering "no such domain" for all of their names.

Settings

Prerequisites

  • off DNS observation: Ad-Block resolver enabled with query logging
  • off DNS blocking: Ad-Block resolver announced to LAN clients (serve_lan)
  • off Clients cannot bypass the resolver with their own DNS server (force_dns)
  • off SNI observation: XDP filter enabled on the LAN-side interfaces with observe_sni

Daemon fr-appid: not running . The XDP filter only sees what an interface receives: attach it to the LAN-side interfaces, not the WAN. It also misses names of 32 characters or more, QUIC (HTTP/3) and Encrypted Client Hello.

FR_OSSystemSystem

System: Post-Quantum Hybrid Key Exchange

Hardens the management layer (this webUI's HTTPS listener, and this host's sshd if installed) with a hybrid classical+PQC key exchange (X25519MLKEM768 for TLS, mlkem768x25519-sha256 for SSH), falling back to classical-only automatically on any client or host build that doesn't support it yet.

Classical only
PQC enabled in config
No
Host OpenSSL
Go crypto/tls (X25519MLKEM768)
SSH installed
No

TLS (webUI HTTPS)

CheckResult
Host OpenSSL supports X25519MLKEM768 (requires OpenSSL ≥ 3.5) Yes
Last applied TLS group preference (never applied)
Hybrid group currently applied No

TLS 1.3 is always enforced when PQC is enabled below. The group preference itself only takes effect on the next apply and a subsequent systemctl restart fr-webui -- OpenSSL reads its configuration once, at process start.

SSH

sshd is not installed on this host -- nothing to configure.

Settings

Never breaks an older client or an older sshd/browser build -- if the host's OpenSSL or OpenSSH is too old to know the hybrid algorithm name, this silently keeps the classical-only fallback list (still TLS 1.3-only on the webUI side) instead of failing.

Management access

The webUI and SSH listen on 127.0.0.1, 192.168.1.1 and are reachable from the lan zone(s). The firewall drops them from wan, whatever the rules say.

To manage the router from outside, turn on the VPN (WireGuard) rather than opening the webUI and SSH to the internet.

Which zones count as management: management.zones in the config (default: every zone that isn't internet-facing).

webUI address

Where the webUI and SSH listen (besides the router itself). Only this setting moves them: a change elsewhere that would take one of these addresses away is refused (ROADMAP SEC-27). Saving applies it at once, held until you confirm it from the new address within 300 s; otherwise the router goes back.

Over IPv6

The webUI and SSH can also listen on the router's stable IPv6 address (ULA) in each management zone that has IPv6 -- never on the provider's addresses, which change and are public. The same rules apply as over IPv4.

IPv6 is off (Interfaces screen).

Software integrity

FR_OS's files -- the program, its compiled files, its systemd units and scripts, the XDP program -- are compared with the signed release they came from (security-lessons G9, ROADMAP SEC-15), so rewriting pip's install record doesn't hide a change. It covers FR_OS's own files only: a change elsewhere -- another systemd unit, another program, an SSH key -- is not reported. Someone with root can still change this check itself: the check that doesn't trust the router reads its boot medium from another computer (scripts/verify-medium.py).

not verifiable FR_OS 2 keeps no list of its files' hashes yet

Storage & persistence

installed This router runs from its own disk; every change is kept.

Multi-site monitoring

A Prometheus server can scrape this router's /metrics over HTTPS. It is off until a token is generated here; then it answers only requests carrying Authorization: Bearer <token> (only its SHA-256 is kept in config.yaml). Examples: telemetry/prometheus-multisite.yml and the fleet dashboard in telemetry/.

# HELP fros_info Constant 1; labels identify this router (site name, hostname, version, release codename).
# TYPE fros_info gauge
fros_info{site_name="edge-gw",hostname="edge-gw",version="0.2.1",codename="Ice Breaker"} 1
# HELP fros_config_valid 1 if the on-disk config.yaml passes validation, else 0.
# TYPE fros_config_valid gauge
fros_config_valid 1
# HELP fros_interface_bytes_total Total bytes transferred per network interface and direction.
# TYPE fros_interface_bytes_total counter
# HELP fros_xdp_status XDP TLS SNI filter attach status per interface (0=disabled/not attached, 1=native, 2=generic).
# TYPE fros_xdp_status gauge
fros_xdp_status{device="eth1"} 0
fros_xdp_status{device="eth2"} 0
# HELP fros_dns_blocked_domains Domains currently loaded into the DNS resolver, per blocklist category.
# TYPE fros_dns_blocked_domains gauge
fros_dns_blocked_domains{category="ads"} 0
fros_dns_blocked_domains{category="malware"} 0
fros_dns_blocked_domains{category="my-list"} 0
# HELP fros_app_active_clients Clients that used the app in the last 15 minutes (DNS lookups / TLS SNIs).
# TYPE fros_app_active_clients gauge
# HELP fros_app_hits_24h DNS lookups and TLS connections attributed to the app in the last 24 hours.
# TYPE fros_app_hits_24h gauge
# HELP fros_app_blocked Apps currently on the blocked list (1 per blocked app).
# TYPE fros_app_blocked gauge
fros_app_blocked{app="tiktok"} 1
# HELP fros_tls_fingerprinted_clients Clients with at least one TLS fingerprint recorded.
# TYPE fros_tls_fingerprinted_clients gauge
fros_tls_fingerprinted_clients 0
# HELP fros_tls_distinct_fingerprints Distinct JA4 fingerprints recorded across all clients.
# TYPE fros_tls_distinct_fingerprints gauge
fros_tls_distinct_fingerprints 0
# HELP fros_tls_fingerprint_events_24h TLS fingerprint events in the last 24 hours, by type.
# TYPE fros_tls_fingerprint_events_24h gauge
fros_tls_fingerprint_events_24h{type="new_fingerprint"} 0
fros_tls_fingerprint_events_24h{type="blocklist"} 0
# HELP fros_adblock_total_domains Number of unique domains currently in the ad-block hosts list.
# TYPE fros_adblock_total_domains gauge
fros_adblock_total_domains 0
# HELP fros_hw_cpu_info CPU model identification (value is always 1).
# TYPE fros_hw_cpu_info gauge
# HELP fros_hw_cpu_usage_ratio Current CPU utilization ratio (0-1), sampled over a short interval.
# TYPE fros_hw_cpu_usage_ratio gauge
# HELP fros_hw_cpu_mhz Current CPU clock speed in MHz.
# TYPE fros_hw_cpu_mhz gauge
# HELP fros_hw_storage_info Mounted storage device identification (value is always 1).
# TYPE fros_hw_storage_info gauge
fros_hw_storage_info{mount="/",device_name="/dev/sda1"} 1
# HELP fros_hw_storage_usage_bytes Used storage space in bytes for this mount.
# TYPE fros_hw_storage_usage_bytes gauge
fros_hw_storage_usage_bytes{mount="/"} 2147483648
# HELP fros_hw_storage_total_bytes Total storage space in bytes for this mount.
# TYPE fros_hw_storage_total_bytes gauge
fros_hw_storage_total_bytes{mount="/"} 8589934592

IPv6

The router takes IPv6 from the provider on its internet-facing interfaces: an address (SLAAC or DHCPv6) and, if the provider delegates one, a prefix. Each LAN zone's interface gets a /64 network of that prefix, which its devices configure themselves from (SLAAC; ipv6.lan_zones chooses the zones, all of them by default). Each also gets a stable network of the router's own (ULA), where the router answers DNS whatever the provider gives. The rules decide what the LAN reaches over IPv6, as over IPv4; nothing new comes in from the internet but through a pinhole (ipv6.pinholes).     zone: iot
    address: 192.168.20.1/24

  wan: {}
  lan: {}
  iot: {}

nat:

  lan:

    dns_servers: [192.168.1.1]

  to_zone: wan

  action: accept

  to_zone: lan

  to_zone: self

  proto: tcp
  dst_port: 5000-5999

  enabled: true
  interfaces: [lan, iot]

XDP TLS SNI Filter

Kernel-space (XDP/eBPF) TLS ClientHello inspection -- drops connections to blocklisted domains before they reach the kernel's normal network stack. What it can't see is listed below, and in bpf/xdp_sni_filter.c -- read that before relying on this as a complete filter.

Native / Driver (xdpdrv)
Interface
lan
Blocked domains
2
Drops (since last load)
17

Attached interfaces

InterfaceDeviceMode
lan eth1 Native / Driver (xdpdrv)
iot eth2 Generic / SKB (xdpgeneric)

What this filter doesn't see

  • QUIC (HTTP/3, UDP/443). Its ClientHello is encrypted. Rejected from eth1, eth2 while the filter is on, so browsers fall back to TLS over TCP, where the name is seen.
  • Encrypted Client Hello (ECH). The real name is encrypted; the filter sees only the outer, public one.
  • TLS on ports other than 443.
  • ClientHellos over several TLS records. They pass, counted as truncated. One split across TCP segments is followed: a segment out of order is dropped until TCP sends it in order, one with a bad checksum is dropped unread, and a hello longer than 16 segments, unfinished after 30 seconds or in a segment over 2,048 bytes is dropped.
  • Names of 32 bytes or more. Refused when you add them, so none is silently ineffective.
  • IPv6 with more than four extension headers, and TCP fragments. The filter reads IPv6 like IPv4, behind up to four extension headers. A packet with more, and a TCP fragment of either family, is dropped instead: no LAN device sends one, and the server would put a hello back together that the filter never saw whole.

Settings

XDP only sees packets an interface receives. To filter what LAN clients connect to, pick the LAN-side interfaces; on the WAN interface it only sees connections coming in from the internet.

Blocking a domain also blocks its subdomains (e.g. "example.com" blocks "www.example.com" too) -- see this project's ARCHITECTURE.md for the LPM-trie matching scheme.

Saving only updates config.yaml -- click Apply on the dashboard to actually load the filter into the kernel.

Evaluated in order, first match wins. "self" as a zone means the router itself. Scheduled drop/reject rules that cut open connections are evaluated before all other rules.

Rule hit counters are recorded hourly (fr-schedule-check.timer); "unused" means no match for 90 days.

FR_OSProtectionTLS SNI Filter

XDP TLS SNI Filter

Kernel-space (XDP/eBPF) TLS ClientHello inspection -- drops connections to blocklisted domains before they reach the kernel's normal network stack. What it can't see is listed below, and in bpf/xdp_sni_filter.c -- read that before relying on this as a complete filter.

Not attached yet -- run Apply
Interface
lan, iot
Blocked domains
2
Drops (since last load)
unavailable -- the apply-helper didn't answer; firewall-cli xdp-status shows them

What this filter doesn't see

  • QUIC (HTTP/3, UDP/443). Its ClientHello is encrypted. Rejected from eth1, eth2 while the filter is on, so browsers fall back to TLS over TCP, where the name is seen.
  • Encrypted Client Hello (ECH). The real name is encrypted; the filter sees only the outer, public one.
  • TLS on ports other than 443.
  • ClientHellos over several TLS records. They pass, counted as truncated. One split across TCP segments is followed: a segment out of order is dropped until TCP sends it in order, one with a bad checksum is dropped unread, and a hello longer than 16 segments, unfinished after 30 seconds or in a segment over 2,048 bytes is dropped.
  • Names of 32 bytes or more. Refused when you add them, so none is silently ineffective.
  • IPv6 with more than four extension headers, and TCP fragments. The filter reads IPv6 like IPv4, behind up to four extension headers. A packet with more, and a TCP fragment of either family, is dropped instead: no LAN device sends one, and the server would put a hello back together that the filter never saw whole.

Settings

XDP only sees packets an interface receives. To filter what LAN clients connect to, pick the LAN-side interfaces; on the WAN interface it only sees connections coming in from the internet.

Blocking a domain also blocks its subdomains (e.g. "example.com" blocks "www.example.com" too) -- see this project's ARCHITECTURE.md for the LPM-trie matching scheme.

Saving only updates config.yaml -- click Apply on the dashboard to actually load the filter into the kernel.

Blocked domains

ads.example.com
tracker.example.net

Live TLS Inspection Logs (40Gbps Wire-Speed Data Plane)

Streamed from fr-xdp-sni-logger's journal as each match is logged -- the drop decision itself already happened in the kernel, entirely independent of this page being open. "40Gbps wire-speed" describes what the native (xdpdrv) data plane is designed for on supported hardware, not a throughput number measured on this box -- see ROADMAP.md's phase 4 open items for real hardware benchmarking status.
